sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Doesn’t need her Signature weapon to perform and easy to build Echoes-wise (good Energy generation).

 Has easy gameplay that benefits from Perfect Dodges (so interruption isn’t a big issue).

 Has access to multiple Echo sets that all work on her to similar effect, making finding Echoes for her really easy.

 Fits into several teams beyond her intended DPS Lucy, can act as a slightly stronger or equal version of Mortefi (an already proven strong 4-star in the meta).

 She’s free!

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Very long rotations compared to the average secondary buffer. Deals more damage than most Hybrids to compensate, but still extends team rotations a good amount.

 Good for a free character, but still a free character. Don’t expect her to shatter the meta; she only brings a good alternative for Heavy Attackers and is only best in slot for an average DPS.

 Ultimate voiceline gets very annoying after a few uses. Kuro Games, please allow us to disable it like Ciaccona’s Ultimate song.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text:
Rebecca is a 5-star Electro Pistols buffer who specializes in dealing Basic Attack damage and buffing Heavy Attacks. She has access to the Hack mechanic, a variant of Tune Rupture, and provides a secondary source of damage as well as Heavy Attack-related buffs to enhance your Main DPS’s firepower as much as possible.
 Key Mechanics & Rotation
 Rebecca has 2 states she can switch between freely in order to complete her rotations: Huntress and Guts. She swaps between them on every Intro and Skill cast, starting in Huntress state. Practically, she will use Guts state to generate most of her Forte gauge, then cast her Forte Heavy Attack in Huntress state and Outro, creating a loop since every rotation starts in Huntress state, switching to Guts upon Intro, then back to Huntress via one Skill, leaving her in Huntress state for the start of every rotation.
 Each state brings small self-buffs to Rebecca, being 30% CRIT DMG and 15% DEF Ignore buffs, where she activates both at once upon casting Intro thanks to her automatically replenished Forte resource, Hot Hand.
 Her manually replenished resource, called Fervor, is charged via her Intro, Basic Attacks and Skill. When fully replenished, she casts a special Forte Heavy Attack, dealing a good amount of damage and restoring a lot of Concerto.
 Rebecca’s Ultimate restores a ton of Concerto and deals a lot of damage as well. It occurs in 3 stages where Rebecca shoots 15 bullets total, progressively getting enhanced as the Basic Attack or Ultimate button is pressed every 5 shots (indicated on her Forte gauge). She then finishes off with a big blast of additional damage and Concerto that can be Swap-cancelled in optimal rotations. It also grants a small 20% ATK buff to the team upon casting.
 Finally, her Outro amplifies All-type DMG and summons a turret that progressively increases the Heavy Attack DMG of the on-field character, the turret dealing constant damage as well. This totals up to 15% General Amplification and 35% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification, giving a maximum of 50% Amplification to Heavy Attackers when the full buffs are acquired (this is instant for Lucy, but takes the full 14s for other characters).
 Additionally, similarly to Lucy, Rebecca has access to a unique Tune Break response called Hack. It functions the same as Tune Rupture, just under a different name, but uses the same scalings and general mechanics otherwise, overall enhancing the damage of your Tune Break Skill casts when applied by several of Rebecca’s attacks.
 As a result, Rebecca’s rotation will have her progressively work up towards her Forte Heavy Attack via 3 Basic Attacks and a Skill before finally casting the Heavy, followed by her Ultimate, and swapping out of her finisher attack (provided enough Concerto has been built ahead of time).
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Rebecca deals good damage and has good Heavy Attack buffing potential. Functionally, in spite of a quite lengthy rotation (over 7 seconds in all situations), she is still an alternative to the already proven meta Heavy Attack buffer, being Mortefi. As they are both free to acquire and have strong Heavy ATK buffing potential and a reliance on the same weapon and Echo set, being Static Mist and Moonlit Clouds, they fulfill the same niche. Disregarding different elements, which may give the advantage to one or the other depending on elemental resistance, Rebecca is generally slightly stronger in all Heavy Attack teams, with characters like Jiyan, Augusta and Phoebe, especially considering when her Signature Weapon is acquired. Obviously, Rebecca is also best used alongside Lucy, with whom she attains very solid performance although not meta-shaping.
 In conclusion, for a free character, Rebecca is quite serviceable, being a “second Mortefi” of sorts who can strongly contribute to your Heavy Attack main damage dealers, having a particularly strong synergy with Lucy for several use cases in all Heavy Attack-based teams in the game. She is strongly recommended to build if you have a valid use case for her on one of your Heavy Attack-based teams, as she works well even without her Signature weapon or extra Sequence nodes, making her accessible and viable, particularly when paired with Lucy if you own her (although that’s not necessary to have her perform well)!

sections.heading: Rotation & Gameplay
sections.text:
Rebecca’s rotation goal, similarly to Lucy, is to build towards her Forte Heavy Attack by quickly building her resource called Fervor. She can then build enough Concerto to use her Ultimate and swap its finisher attack at the end of her rotation. It’s possible to create a rotation where Rebecca can swap out of her Ultimate’s finisher attack on the first rotation, called “Boom! Fireworks”, by generating more Concerto than would be necessary. Due to the swap cancel, this will then carry over 10 Concerto Energy into the next rotation, for her to keep repeating this without needing to cast any extra attacks to build additional Concerto on any rotation that follows. This is Rebecca’s main optimization and a significant time save. This, however, means her first rotation looks different than any subsequent rotation, like so:

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Yangyang Xuanling Lucy - yangyang-xuanling is the highest Heavy Attack damage dealer in the game. It's no surprise that Rebecca's best team is alongside her as she is her best Heavy Attack DMG buffer, on par with the generalist top tier Lynae.  Review
 Rebecca is a 5-star Electro Pistols buffer who specializes in dealing Basic Attack damage and buffing Heavy Attacks. She has access to the Hack mechanic, a variant of Tune Rupture, and provides a secondary source of damage as well as Heavy Attack-related buffs to enhance your Main DPS’s firepower as much as possible.
 Key Mechanics & Rotation
 Rebecca has 2 states she can switch between freely in order to complete her rotations: Huntress and Guts. She swaps between them on every Intro and Skill cast, starting in Huntress state. Practically, she will use Guts state to generate most of her Forte gauge, then cast her Forte Heavy Attack in Huntress state and Outro, creating a loop since every rotation starts in Huntress state, switching to Guts upon Intro, then back to Huntress via one Skill, leaving her in Huntress state for the start of every rotation.
 Each state brings small self-buffs to Rebecca, being 30% CRIT DMG and 15% DEF Ignore buffs, where she activates both at once upon casting Intro thanks to her automatically replenished Forte resource, Hot Hand.
 Her manually replenished resource, called Fervor, is charged via her Intro, Basic Attacks and Skill. When fully replenished, she casts a special Forte Heavy Attack, dealing a good amount of damage and restoring a lot of Concerto.
 Rebecca’s Ultimate restores a ton of Concerto and deals a lot of damage as well. It occurs in 3 stages where Rebecca shoots 15 bullets total, progressively getting enhanced as the Basic Attack or Ultimate button is pressed every 5 shots (indicated on her Forte gauge). She then finishes off with a big blast of additional damage and Concerto that can be Swap-cancelled in optimal rotations. It also grants a small 20% ATK buff to the team upon casting.
 Finally, her Outro amplifies All-type DMG and summons a turret that progressively increases the Heavy Attack DMG of the on-field character, the turret dealing constant damage as well. This totals up to 15% General Amplification and 35% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification, giving a maximum of 50% Amplification to Heavy Attackers when the full buffs are acquired (this is instant for Lucy, but takes the full 14s for other characters).
 Additionally, similarly to Lucy, Rebecca has access to a unique Tune Break response called Hack. It functions the same as Tune Rupture, just under a different name, but uses the same scalings and general mechanics otherwise, overall enhancing the damage of your Tune Break Skill casts when applied by several of Rebecca’s attacks.
 As a result, Rebecca’s rotation will have her progressively work up towards her Forte Heavy Attack via 3 Basic Attacks and a Skill before finally casting the Heavy, followed by her Ultimate, and swapping out of her finisher attack (provided enough Concerto has been built ahead of time).
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Rebecca deals good damage and has good Heavy Attack buffing potential. Functionally, in spite of a quite lengthy rotation (over 7 seconds in all situations), she is still an alternative to the already proven meta Heavy Attack buffer, being Mortefi. As they are both free to acquire and have strong Heavy ATK buffing potential and a reliance on the same weapon and Echo set, being Static Mist and Moonlit Clouds, they fulfill the same niche. Disregarding different elements, which may give the advantage to one or the other depending on elemental resistance, Rebecca is generally slightly stronger in all Heavy Attack teams, with characters like Jiyan, Augusta and Phoebe, especially considering when her Signature Weapon is acquired. Obviously, Rebecca is also best used alongside Lucy, with whom she attains very solid performance although not meta-shaping.
 In conclusion, for a free character, Rebecca is quite serviceable, being a “second Mortefi” of sorts who can strongly contribute to your Heavy Attack main damage dealers, having a particularly strong synergy with Lucy for several use cases in all Heavy Attack-based teams in the game. She is strongly recommended to build if you have a valid use case for her on one of your Heavy Attack-based teams, as she works well even without her Signature weapon or extra Sequence nodes, making her accessible and viable, particularly when paired with Lucy if you own her (although that’s not necessary to have her perform well)!

 Rotation & Gameplay
 Rebecca’s rotation goal, similarly to Lucy, is to build towards her Forte Heavy Attack by quickly building her resource called Fervor. She can then build enough Concerto to use her Ultimate and swap its finisher attack at the end of her rotation. It’s possible to create a rotation where Rebecca can swap out of her Ultimate’s finisher attack on the first rotation, called “Boom! Fireworks”, by generating more Concerto than would be necessary. Due to the swap cancel, this will then carry over 10 Concerto Energy into the next rotation, for her to keep repeating this without needing to cast any extra attacks to build additional Concerto on any rotation that follows.
